newsitem.title: UK: Bjork very distressed by acid bomb attempt - manager.
newsitem.headline: Bjork very distressed by acid bomb attempt - manager.

text.p: Rock singer Bjork is "very distressed" by the suicide of a Florida man after he sent her an bomb designed to spray her with sulphuric acid, her manager said on Wednesday.

The body of Ricardo Lopez, 21, was found on the floor of his Florida apartment on Monday after neighbours reported a foul odour. He had shot himself in the head with a .38 calibre revolver, police said on Tuesday.
He mailed the device to the Icelandic singer but it was located by police at a post office in London early on Tuesday and detonated without incident.

Speaking outside Bjork's house in west London, manager Derek Birkett said she had been advised by police not to talk to the press. "Although she had never met or spoken to the individual concerned, she is naturally very distressed to hear about his death," he said.

After seeing Bjork's son Sindri on to his school bus this morning, Birkett said: "There was never any question the bomb would get through, the police are very good about that sort of thing, especially in England."

He said the device had been sent to Bjork care of her management company. "Nothing like this has happened to her before. I told her what had happened and she was very distressed. I don't know why she attracts this sort of thing."
Investigators said an 8 mm video camera on a tripod was pointed at Lopez's body and 11 video tapes were found, including one labeled "Last Day - Ricardo Lopez."
The video showed Lopez "meticulously" constructing a chemical propulsion device and also showed him killing himself.

"Apparently he was obsessed with alternative rock singer Bjork Gudmonsdottir and that led to his creating a device that he was going to mail to her and in fact did mail to her," said Hollywood police spokesman Todd DeAngelis. "She was going to open it and presumably be harmed by that."
Gudmonsdottir, who is known by the single name Bjork, is former lead singer for the Sugar Cubes and now performs solo.
The Florida investigators learned the address to which the device had been sent by viewing the videotapes and contacted Scotland Yard, which tracked down the package at a post office in south London.
